subject: Cognito Labs — renewal capacity & headroom preflight
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cognitolabs.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, purchasing <purchasing@cognitolabs.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity headroom and ROI for Q1

Hi Naomi / Ben —

As we approach our December renewal window I wanted to surface Cognito's usage trends and get aligned on options to cover anticipated growth. High level: token run-rate has increased ~48% month-over-month after we shipped the new search augmentation feature (peak seq length higher, more streaming calls). We expect a sustained +30% baseline uptick over the next 12 months.

Can you share a short health summary (token burn, p95 latency shifts, any model mix changes) and an idea for a term/commit structure that keeps unit cost predictable while giving us burst headroom for spikes? Procurement wants a recommended option by next Tuesday.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

—Marta
Head of Product Ops
Cognito Labs

[Attachment: usage_snapshot_summary.xlsx (XLSX, 38KB)]

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cognitolabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity headroom and ROI for Q1

Marta — thanks for the signal and the spreadsheet. Quick take after a first-pass review:

- Token trajectory: Q3 -> Q4 growth driven by search augmentation equals ~48% MoM at peak; trailing 14-day run-rate shows a smoothed +27% uplift.
- Model mix: 62% of requests moved from the smaller gen-7 family to the gen-8 medium variant for better context handling; gen-9 is used only for long-form generation (2% of tokens).
- Latency: p95 for gen-8 increased from 220ms to 380ms in peak windows; p50 roughly unchanged. We see increased cold-starts on the dedicated inference nodes during batched ETL windows.

Recommendation (short): a 12-month term with a 25% committed uplift over current annualized run-rate, plus a 20% burst pool for peak-days. This preserves a lower per-token rate and buys predictable capacity. We can include an automatic prefetch/batching configuration (prefetch window + KV cache TTL) to recover ~8–12% of token burn on prefix-heavy calls.

I'm attaching the usage export and our latency bench. I'll follow with a proposed term sheet and three pricing tiers (conservative / target / aggressive).

Next steps: I can share the term summary today and set up a 30-min preflight with procurement Monday.

—Naomi
Customer Success Manager 
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: cognito_q3_usage.csv (CSV, 42KB)]
[Attachment: latency_benchmarks_q3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

From: Jared Li <jared.li@cognitolabs.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cognitolabs.com>, purchasing <purchasing@cognitolabs.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity headroom and ROI for Q1

Naomi — appreciate the quick read. Couple clarifying Qs from procurement side: 

1) For the 20% burst pool, how is that charged during sustained bursts (e.g., 3 consecutive days)? Any throttling or spillover rules we should expect?
2) Can you quantify the expected token-savings range from the prefetch + KV cache changes (best / likely / worst)? We need ranges for our internal TCO model.

If you can include a sample DocuSign-ready term we can fast-track approvals. Ideally procurement wants optionality for a 6-month pilot at a slightly higher per-token rate as a lower-risk path.

—Jared
Director, Infrastructure
Cognito Labs

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jared Li <jared.li@cognitolabs.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cognitolabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity headroom and ROI for Q1

Jared — answers inline: 

1) Burst pool mechanics: the 20% burst pool is billed at the committed rate for the first 72 hours of contiguous increased usage; if sustained beyond 72 hours we transition to the on-demand rate for overflow. We can add a hard cap and an opt-in throttling policy if you prefer guaranteed latency over completing every request.

2) Prefetch/KV cache savings (empirical ranges from similar customers):
- Best: 18–22% token reduction (prefix-heavy, stable prompts)
- Likely: 8–12% token reduction (mixed traffic)
- Worst: 3–5% token reduction (high variety, short prompts)

Attached is a 1-page term summary (three options). Option A (12m, +25% commit, 20% burst) is our recommended path; Option B is a 6m pilot at +10% commit with slightly higher unit price; Option C is a 12m conservative (no burst pool) for procurement comfort.

I also created a DocuSign link for Option A so you can review the legal language quickly: https://www.docusign.com/CL-2027-TERM-PROP

If Cognito wants the pilot route we can convert to Option B and include a free one-month burst credit to demonstrate headroom.

—Naomi

[Attachment: proposed_term_summary.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)]

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Nov 2027 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Cognito Labs — renewal capacity & headroom preflight

Naomi / Ben — looping in legal and pricing. Naomi, thanks for the good options. Two internal asks before we send the final: 1) can you add a short annex that defines the throttling policy and the exact overflow billing rule (we should be explicit: 72 hours continuous -> overflow billed at on-demand rate; hard cap opt-in), and 2) a short example monthly invoice showing committed vs burst usage math for the recommended Option A.

I'll coordinate with Legal on the DocuSign template once we have those two items. Also confirm whether the prefetch recommendation needs any runtime changes on their side (it should be safe but call it out).

—Priyom
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
